column1: # source: von Seth, Aller & Davis 2025, Unimodal speech perception predicts stable individual differences in audiovisual benefit for phonemes, words and sentences, JASA 157(3):1554-1576, doi:10.1121/10.0034846; preprint PsyArXiv doi:10.31234/osf.io/kj59f; data OSF https://osf.io/j56y4/ files data/scored_data/consonants_scored.xlsx (session 1) and consonants_scored_2.xlsx (session 2), downloaded 2026-10-15; counted by trial here (the paper prints no matrix, only feature transmission).

# condition: audiovisual (talking face + sound), low clarity (p=0: 1-channel noise vocoding, broadband envelope only); not masked by noise. Overall 55.4% correct (4780 trials). 20-alternative forced choice (closed set, response words bad chat dad fat get hat jet cat let met net pet rat shed tad that vet wet yet zed); no /s/ stimulus or response.

# 126 normal-hearing native British English adults online (session 1: 126, session 2: 113 of them; all released trials pooled, 239 per consonant per condition; the files label both sessions "Session_2", the session is taken from the file), 1 female talker, consonant + /ə/ from a closed-mouth start; each consonant once per condition per session. Rows = sent, columns = heard, counts. y = /j/, dj = /dZ/, ch = /tS/, sh = /S/, th = /T/.
